title: Microrequest canvas + priority notes — Mar 2029
body:
Purpose
---
This is a lightweight, tactical canvas that compiles high-frequency microrequests from frontline CS conversations (Jan–Mar 2029), groups them by suggested remediation pattern, and proposes short technical or config-level fixes we can ship in a 2–6 week window. The intent is: 1) surface small items that unblock customers quickly, 2) reduce repeated CS toil, 3) capture impact / rollback risk, and 4) hand off to eng squads with clear acceptance criteria.

Notes on scope and constraints
---
- "Microrequest" = request that does not require a full product spec or multi-month commit (examples: routing tweak, default timeout change, telemetry flag, helper doc + CLI sample).
- Prioritization leans toward fixes that reduce repeated CS effort and those that materially improve latency/cost for paying Dedicated customers.
- Avoid items that require model architecture changes or major infra rework. Those are captured elsewhere.

High-level themes observed (top-of-mind)
---
1) Routing transparency gaps: customers see fallback model responses without clear logs about why routing fired (region capacity vs. cost-tier routing).
2) Cold-start tail latency for small-burst workloads: single-request SLO regressions when VMs spin up, especially on Dedicated with burst enabled.
3) Embedding batch size defaults are too aggressive for low-volume customers, causing latency for real-time inference use cases.
4) Eval/quality rollback friction: teams want an easier, non-prod path to run prompt regression checks against canary model variants.
5) Billing signal confusion: per-token vs. per-request attribution not shown in a single view for multi-model pipelines.

Microrequest entries (prioritized)
---
1) 'Routing rationale' header in request logs
- Ask: Add a lightweight "routing_rationale" field to request logs and console trace that indicates which policy matched (latency-first / cost-first / pinned) and whether fallback happened.
- Source: 8 accounts (CS notes Feb–Mar) complaining about unexplained fallbacks during business hours.
- Impact: Medium-high (reduces investigation time, lowers escalations).
- Effort estimate: 1 engineer (backend) + 1 observability engineer, ~2 weeks to add, tests and rollout.
- Rollback risk: Low. Non-invasive telemetry addition.
- Acceptance criteria: logs include policy_id, matched_rule, fallback_boolean; Console shows last-5 routing decisions for a given API key.
- Owner suggestion: eng-platform / observability.

2) Default embedding batch cap for realtime routes
- Ask: Introduce per-route default max_batch_size=8 for embedding endpoints flagged as "realtime"; preserve current defaults for batch pipelines.
- Source: 5 customers using streaming UIs where embeddings for single user actions are timing out.
- Impact: High for UX in low-latency embedding use cases; may slightly increase per-token cost but improves perceived responsiveness.
- Effort estimate: config + routing change + docs: ~1 week.
- Rollback risk: Medium (could increase cost). Provide an opt-out flag.
- Acceptance criteria: new default applied to routes labeled realtime; telemetry shows median latency drop and cost delta per customer.
- Owner suggestion: eng-serving-runtime + product-hosted-api.

3) Cold VM warmup policy toggle (Dedicated)
- Ask: Add a per-tenant toggle to prefer keep-warm instances for small burst windows (e.g., pre-warm 1 small instance when sustained request rate < threshold but recent bursts occurred).
- Source: Dedicated customers experiencing 95th percentile tail latency during first 30s of a burst.
- Impact: High for Dedicated customers with spiky traffic; reduces SLA complaints.
- Effort estimate: 2–3 engineers (infra + autoscale) ~3–4 weeks including safety controls.
- Rollback risk: Medium-high (cost impact if misconfigured).
- Mitigations: default off; cost-estimation UI and opt-in.
- Acceptance criteria: metrics show reduction in cold-start tail P95 for opt-in tenants with acceptably bounded cost.
- Owner suggestion: infra / dedicated-squad.

4) One-click canary eval runner (non-prod)
- Ask: Provide a console action to run a small set of pre-registered prompt sets against a candidate model variant (no billing to prod) and show quality delta vs. baseline.
- Source: recurring ask from two enterprise customers and internal AE/SE teams to avoid rolling variants that regress outputs.
- Impact: High (reduces bad rollouts, manual eval effort).
- Effort estimate: 2 engineers + 1 UX over 4–6 weeks for an MVP (can be limited to text-gen only initially).
- Rollback risk: Low.
- Acceptance criteria: console button available under model version page, runs <100 prompts, presents precision/recall-style summary + sample failures.
- Owner suggestion: product-console + applied-ml.

5) Billing attribution helper for multi-model flows
- Ask: Add a simple export that attributes tokens and embed units to pipeline stage and model version (CSV) for the last 30d; include sample queries to reproduce map in BigQuery.
- Source: Finance/ops ask from 3 mid-market customers reconciling invoices.
- Impact: Medium. Reduces finance disputes and support load.
- Effort estimate: 1 engineer (analytics) ~1 week + docs.
- Rollback risk: Low.
- Acceptance criteria: CSV produced with model_version, pipeline_stage, tokens_consumed, cost_estimate.
- Owner suggestion: product-ops + finance-analytics.

Small quick wins (1–3 days)
---
- Add a short FAQ snippet in onboarding: "Why did my request fall back to model X?" with pointer to current routing policies (owner: docs + devex).
- Add a CLI sample for running an embedding one-off with smaller batch sizes (owner: devx).
- Create a templated support reply for "billing attribution for multi-model pipelines" (owner: CS).

Open questions and tradeoffs
---
- For the cold warmup toggle: what guardrails on cost must be required before enabling for an enterprise? (proposal: default budget cap + weekly cost estimate email).
- For the routing rationale logs: how to surface sensitive policy names for customers on private deployments? Need security review.
- For canary eval runner: should we charge for CPU/QA cycles used by customer runs, or provide as a free safety feature? (proposal: free up to 100 prompts / month per org).

Suggested next steps (owners & timeline)
---
Week 0 (this doc): triage with product and infra to confirm prioritization.
Week 1–2: ship quick wins (FAQ snippet, CLI sample, templated support reply).
Week 2–6: routing_rationale + embedding default change (small eng effort parallelized).
Week 3–8: design + spec for cold-warmup toggle; decide opt-in and billing guardrails.
Week 4–10: prototype one-click canary eval runner (MVP limited to text-gen).

Decision log needed: record authorization for changes which increase customer cost (embedding default, warmup policy).

Hand-off notes for engineering squads
---
- Provide a minimal reproducible test plan for each microrequest (CS to capture one customer example with logs).
- Attach suggested telemetry keys: api_key_hash, route_id, model_variant, matched_policy, fallback_flag, latency_ms.
- CS will prioritize customers that will pilot changes (we can ship feature behind opt-in for safety).

Appendix: representative customer snippets
---
- "We had three fallbacks in the middle of the day and nothing in our console said why. Took us two hours to find a capacity blip." — Platform lead, fintech startup (Tier B).
- "Embeddings are fast on our dev machine but in prod each single-click takes 800ms and users notice." — Product PM, B2B SaaS.
- "We'd love a way to sanity-check a candidate model without rolling it to prod; our legal team wants a record." — Head of ML Engineering, health customer.

Notes to reviewer
---
- This is intentionally tactical; for any microrequest that grows beyond two sprints we should move it into the product roadmap with a formal PRD.
- Please flag any data residency or security constraints we should consider before adding telemetry fields.

Action items for CS (owners in parentheses)
---
- Collect 1–2 concrete customer logs that show routing fallback for each tenant (Liam).
- Draft FAQ + CLI sample + support template (Zoe + Dana).
- Coordinate pilot list for warmup toggle (Maya).
summary: Tactical compilation of high-frequency microrequests from CS Jan–Mar 2029. Prioritized five fixes (routing logs, embedding default, warmup toggle, canary eval runner, billing attribution export) with estimates, risks, and acceptance criteria. Includes quick wins, open questions, pilot plan, and CS handoff tasks.
